{{Short description|Mathematical estimate for exponential sums}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Hua's lemma''',<ref>{{cite journal |author=Hua Loo-keng |authorlink=Hua Luogeng |year=1938 |title=On Waring's problem |journal=Quarterly Journal of Mathematics |volume=9 |issue=1 |pages=199–202 |doi=10.1093/qmath/os-9.1.199 |doi-access=free }}</ref> named for [[Hua Loo-keng]], is an estimate for [[exponential sum]]s.

It states that if ''P'' is an [[integral-valued polynomial]] of degree ''k'', <math>\varepsilon</math> is a positive real number, and ''f'' a real function defined by

:<math>f(\alpha)=\sum_{x=1}^N\exp(2\pi iP(x)\alpha),</math>

then

:<math>\int_0^1|f(\alpha)|^\lambda d\alpha\ll_{P, \varepsilon} N^{\mu(\lambda)}</math>,

where <math>(\lambda,\mu(\lambda))</math> lies on a polygonal line with vertices

:<math>(2^\nu,2^\nu-\nu+\varepsilon),\quad\nu=1,\ldots,k.</math>
